Worked Demonstration

Example 1. Green CI, blocked release

User question. Northstar asks whether to release a candidate whose automated suite passed.

Approved reference. An open critical authorization finding blocks release independently of the CI score.

Actual LLM response. The fictional candidate’s CI reports PASS. A separately verified finding shows an unresolved unauthorized refund path.

Assessment. BLOCK. Link the finding to its receipt and the authorization owner. Repair the path and add the incident shape to the next dataset revision.

Failure classification. Confirmed governance blocker outside the scenarios measured by the green CI gate.

Example 2. Approve only a limited rollout

User question. Can Northstar start a canary at 5%?

Approved reference. Require passing comparable evaluation, complete receipts, no blocking findings, a tested return path, monitoring and explicit authority for the candidate and scope.

Actual LLM response. Synthetic refund and privacy controls pass. Priya signs the 5% scope as release approver after the operator verifies the rollback target.

Assessment. APPROVE LIMITED ROLLOUT. At 5%, verify the authorized scope and evaluate the first window before requesting further approval.

Failure classification. No release blocker in this packet. Full rollout needs separate evidence and approval.

Example 3. Roll back after a severe canary event

User question. Should the rollout proceed after the first canary window looks healthy and the next includes an unauthorized refund?

Approved reference. One confirmed unauthorized execution triggers rollback. The previously approved version must be available and verified.

Actual LLM response. The fictional assistant reports a denial. A matched backend receipt and independent ledger show one execution.

Assessment. Stop candidate exposure and restore northstar-v1 in the simulation. Record the trigger, incident evidence, who acted and the independent restoration check. Notify the incident lead, security owner and release owner.

Failure classification. Critical post-release incident. Add the captured case to regression evaluation and require a fresh approval for any repair.

Hands-On Python Exercise

Setup and run

Use Copy Code, open the linked online editor, paste and run. Predict the result before opening Expected output. Change only the specified line, rerun and explain the engineering action. All data are inline, all activities use standard-library Python, and no system is deployed.

Step 1 — Build a release evidence checklist

A dictionary groups names and their evidence status. .items() supplies each name and value to a list comprehension. The condition keeps only missing items.

Open Python Editor

rollback = True
evidence = {"evaluation manifest": True, "CI gate": True, "critical cases": True,
            "security findings reviewed": True, "monitoring": True,
            "rollback": rollback, "approval owner": True}
missing = [name for name, present in evidence.items() if not present]
print("Incomplete evidence:", ", ".join(missing) or "none")
print("Readiness:", "REVIEW" if missing else "CHECKLIST COMPLETE")
Expected output
Incomplete evidence: none
Readiness: CHECKLIST COMPLETE

Experiment. Set rollback = False. Predict which prerequisite remains unsatisfied.

Expected output
Incomplete evidence: rollback
Readiness: REVIEW

Investigate and decide. The passing gate is still visible. Request a rollback rehearsal record before customer exposure.

Step 2 — Validate a release policy

A policy identifies its approved version and conditions. == compares values and all requires every condition to hold.

Open Python Editor

record_version = "release-policy-v1"
policy = {"version": "release-policy-v1", "checks": ["CI", "monitoring", "rollback"]}
record = {"version": record_version, "CI": True, "monitoring": True, "rollback": True}
if record["version"] != policy["version"]:
    result = "INVALID EVIDENCE"
elif all(record[key] for key in policy["checks"]):
    result = "POLICY CHECKS COMPLETE"
else:
    result = "REVIEW"
print("Record policy:", record["version"])
print("Result:", result)
Expected output
Record policy: release-policy-v1
Result: POLICY CHECKS COMPLETE

Experiment. Set record_version = 'release-policy-v2'. Predict whether a passing CI record can still authorize review under v1.

Expected output
Record policy: release-policy-v2
Result: INVALID EVIDENCE

Investigate and decide. The policy identities differ. Recover the authorized record or rerun under the correct rules.

Step 3 — Evaluate residual risk

A list holds finding dictionaries. Every record carries severity, status, mitigation, evidence, owner and optional expiry. and combines severity and status checks.

Open Python Editor

add_critical = False
findings = [{"id": "R-delay", "severity": "low", "status": "accepted",
             "mitigation": "human fallback", "evidence": "fixture://delay",
             "owner": "support", "expires": 20}]
if add_critical:
    findings.append({"id": "F-auth", "severity": "critical", "status": "open",
                     "mitigation": "pending", "evidence": "fixture://receipt",
                     "owner": "security", "expires": None})
blocked = [item["id"] for item in findings
           if item["severity"] == "critical" and item["status"] == "open"]
print("Blocking findings:", ", ".join(blocked) or "none")
print("Decision:", "BLOCK" if blocked else "RISK CHECK COMPLETE")
Expected output
Blocking findings: none
Decision: RISK CHECK COMPLETE

Experiment. Set add_critical = True to add an unresolved authorization finding.

Expected output
Blocking findings: F-auth
Decision: BLOCK

Investigate and decide. The delay risk can be tracked under its documented limited acceptance. The new critical finding forces BLOCK.

Step 4 — Validate approval authority

Check a signed fictional approval against a role registry. .get supplies a default for unknown identities. A scoped approval must cover the requested percentage and come from a different person than the author.

Open Python Editor

signer = "priya"
role_and_limit = {"priya": ("release-approver", 5), "developer": ("author", 0)}
role, maximum = role_and_limit.get(signer, ("unknown", 0))
allowed = role == "release-approver" and maximum >= 5 and signer != "developer"
print("Signer:", signer, "| scope: 5%")
print("Approval:", "VALID" if allowed else "REJECTED")
Expected output
Signer: priya | scope: 5%
Approval: VALID

Experiment. Set signer = 'developer'. Predict whether the release can advance.

Expected output
Signer: developer | scope: 5%
Approval: REJECTED

Investigate and decide. The author has no authority for this sign-off. Ask the release owner for an independent approver.

Step 5 — Plan a staged rollout

List each stage and its required criteria. A set subtraction finds unmet criteria. break stops the loop at the first incomplete stage.

Open Python Editor

monitor_ready = True
ready = {"internal checks", "5% approval"} | ({"monitoring"} if monitor_ready else set())
stages = [("internal", {"internal checks"}), ("5% canary", {"monitoring", "5% approval"}),
          ("25% rollout", {"clean canary", "25% approval"}),
          ("full rollout", {"clean 25% window", "full approval"})]
for name, required in stages:
    gap = sorted(required - ready)
    print(name + ": " + ("WAIT for " + ", ".join(gap) if gap else "READY"))
    if gap:
        break
Expected output
internal: READY
5% canary: READY
25% rollout: WAIT for 25% approval, clean canary

Experiment. Set monitor_ready = False. Predict the furthest permitted stage.

Expected output
internal: READY
5% canary: WAIT for monitoring

Investigate and decide. Internal rehearsal can still be ready. Exposure stops before the 5% canary until monitoring is restored.

Step 6 — Evaluate rollback triggers

Compare counts and rates from one canary window. if and elif stop at the first applicable rule. A confirmed critical event has priority over rate and evidence warnings.

Open Python Editor

unauthorized = 0
privacy_incidents, missing_receipts, errors, requests = 0, 0, 2, 100
if unauthorized or privacy_incidents:
    action = "ROLLBACK"
elif missing_receipts or requests < 50 or errors / requests > 0.04:
    action = "PAUSE"
else:
    action = "CONTINUE AT 5%"
print(f"Errors: {errors}/{requests}, unauthorized: {unauthorized}")
print("Action:", action)
Expected output
Errors: 2/100, unauthorized: 0
Action: CONTINUE AT 5%

Experiment. Set unauthorized = 1. Keep the error rate at 2%.

Expected output
Errors: 2/100, unauthorized: 1
Action: ROLLBACK

Investigate and decide. The ordinary rate still looks healthy, but the confirmed authorization violation triggers rollback.

Step 7 — Generate a release decision record

Use json.dumps with sorted keys to print a machine-readable record. The policy version, actor, scope and evidence travel with the decision.

Open Python Editor

import json

role = "release-approver"
record = {"release_id": "R-42", "candidate": "northstar-v2", "baseline": "northstar-v1",
          "evaluation_manifest": "EVAL-2", "ci": "PASS", "release_policy": "release-policy-v1",
          "residual_risks": ["accepted clarification delay"], "approval": {"role": role, "scope": 5},
          "rollout_percent": 5, "monitoring": "ready", "rollback": "tested",
          "evidence_refs": ["fixture://EVAL-2", "fixture://rollback"]}
record["decision"] = "APPROVE LIMITED ROLLOUT" if role == "release-approver" else "REVIEW"
print(json.dumps(record, sort_keys=True))
Expected output
{"approval": {"role": "release-approver", "scope": 5}, "baseline": "northstar-v1", "candidate": "northstar-v2", "ci": "PASS", "decision": "APPROVE LIMITED ROLLOUT", "evaluation_manifest": "EVAL-2", "evidence_refs": ["fixture://EVAL-2", "fixture://rollback"], "monitoring": "ready", "release_id": "R-42", "release_policy": "release-policy-v1", "residual_risks": ["accepted clarification delay"], "rollback": "tested", "rollout_percent": 5}

Experiment. Set role = 'developer'. Predict the decision while leaving CI and readiness unchanged.

Expected output
{"approval": {"role": "developer", "scope": 5}, "baseline": "northstar-v1", "candidate": "northstar-v2", "ci": "PASS", "decision": "REVIEW", "evaluation_manifest": "EVAL-2", "evidence_refs": ["fixture://EVAL-2", "fixture://rollback"], "monitoring": "ready", "release_id": "R-42", "release_policy": "release-policy-v1", "residual_risks": ["accepted clarification delay"], "rollback": "tested", "rollout_percent": 5}

Investigate and decide. The same technical evidence remains valid. The release needs an authorized independent sign-off.

Real Release Governance Workflow

Review the release packet
  1. Freeze the candidate, previously approved configuration, intended scope and release policy. Retrieve the evaluation and CI reports from their trusted store, validate their versions and digests, and check pairing, coverage, critical cases and receipts.
  2. Review open findings, privacy and security controls, retained data and residual risks. Escalate non-waivable defects. Review exception requests with an accountable owner, approval and expiry. Verify that the person approving the release has authority for its scope and is independent where policy requires it.
  3. Confirm internal and shadow readiness, the monitored cohort, alert owner, explicit thresholds, runbook, tested return path and target configuration. Generate a recommendation and obtain a version-bound approval. Archive the packet, human decision, reasons, time and permitted exposure.
Operate and learn
  1. Begin the authorized stage. Observe linked canary signals and their denominators. Continue within scope if the window passes. Pause for inadequate evidence or a noncritical threshold breach. For a confirmed critical signal, stop exposure and restore the verified target, or isolate the candidate while the return path is investigated.
  2. Keep the incident evidence, triggering window, previous and restored version, operator, notifications and verification of restored behavior. Assess affected writes or disclosures separately.
  3. If the candidate changes materially, generate new evaluation evidence and request fresh approval. Update the regression dataset, rebaseline if the policy or evaluator changed, close or renew exceptions through their owner, and record the lessons and monitoring follow-up.
Illustrative GitHub governance workflow

Required status checks can enforce a CI condition for merging. Review the trusted check source and the required policy in repository settings. For example, keep the previous lesson’s offline evaluation check required and route missing evidence to REVIEW. A green check provides one input to governance.

GitHub environments can protect a job with reviewers, branch or tag rules, and other safeguards where the repository plan and visibility support them. Required reviewers permit one listed reviewer to advance a job. Enable prevention of self-review if it is part of your policy. If Northstar requires separate risk and release sign-offs, validate the risk sign-off in the packet and enforce the independent release approval through the supported controls. Review bypass settings and permissions.

The example below illustrates jobs.<job_id>.environment in a training repository. The manual event would dispatch an evidence-review job. The job prints a fixed message after any configured environment protections allow it. It deploys no application and needs no token permissions beyond the empty permissions mapping. Keep this as documentation. An environment named in a real workflow can create or record deployment activity even when the referenced job has no deployment command. Preconfigure the intended training environment and protections before relying on a hosted approval.

name: Northstar evidence review example
'on': workflow_dispatch
permissions: {}
jobs:
  evidence-review:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    environment:
      name: northstar-training-review
    steps:
      - name: Acknowledge reviewed packet
        run: echo "Review the signed scope in the release packet."

In a real governance process, use GitHub deployment activity to correlate an environment job, source revision and status with your own release ID. A completed environment job tells the reviewer that a workflow step ran. Check the traffic flag and observe a request on the approved route to confirm which version is serving. Preserve both the process record and the observed result. Retain restricted links to the signed scope and redacted supporting artifacts. Keep approvals, final rollout status and any rollback record even if the report was later corrected. Official references are https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/workflows-and-actions/deployments-and-environments, https://docs.github.com/en/actions/how-tos/deploy/configure-and-manage-deployments/manage-environments and https://docs.github.com/en/repositories/configuring-branches-and-merges-in-your-repository/managing-protected-branches/about-protected-branches.

For an evaluation evidence artifact, the documented promptfoo eval --output northstar-results.json exports results from an already configured, authorized suite. Read case outcomes and execution errors, retain the export version and checksum, and bind it to the release run contract. Save only approved data. The report cannot provide release authority. See https://www.promptfoo.dev/docs/configuration/outputs/. The illustrative YAML was parsed locally. Hosted Actions and Promptfoo execution, deployment and live-model behavior remain unverified. The lab below is a complete offline substitute.

Practice Exercises

Practice 1. Block despite green CI

The gate passes all frozen critical cases, but an independent review found an open critical authorization defect. Name the evidence that takes priority and describe the retest.

Practice 2. Verify the signer

Evaluation, monitoring and rollback evidence is complete. The candidate’s developer is the only person who signed. Decide whether the system can be exposed and what sign-off must replace this one.

Practice 3. Respect the canary ceiling

Priya signed 5% scope. The canary has just started. A teammate requests 100% immediately. Explain which independent evidence and authority are missing.

Practice 4. Contain a confirmed severe incident

The canary has 2/100 ordinary errors and one confirmed unauthorized write. State the operational action and notification list, and describe how to verify restoration and handle the completed write.

Independent Assignment

Use the full lab program as your standalone runner. Verify the manifest, CI result, release policy and records. Review critical and residual risks, exceptions, approval, monitoring and rollback plans. Submit a short explanation of the decision, the permitted scope and the next concrete action. Turn SHOW_JSON on to inspect the decision record and archived approvals.

Variant A sets MODE = "wide_scope". A signer with authority for wider scope signs 25%, but this is still an initial rollout. Explain the gate that prevents expansion. Variant B sets MODE = "wrong_evaluator". The CI record is internally linked to a manifest using evaluator-v2. Explain why the packet is invalid for this release policy even when CI is green. Run both variants from clean copies of the same complete program.

Worked Solutions to Practice

Solution 1

The independent confirmed finding is a blocker even though the automated suite reports PASS. Record BLOCK and retain both evidence sources. Route the finding to the authorization owner. Verify the repaired deny path and a permitted control, add the incident shape to the regression dataset, and require a new run and sign-off.

Solution 2

The developer cannot fulfill the documented independence requirement. Return REVIEW without exposing the candidate. Ask an authorized reviewer to sign the candidate, configuration digest, evaluation, policy and exact scope. Check the signer’s identity, role assignment and time against the packet before allowing rollout.

Solution 3

The 5% approval binds the canary ceiling. Collect a complete observation window, reconcile all critical receipts and confirm the rate is within policy. Request a new approval before 25% and later before 100% under the rollout plan. Validate the new scope against the same candidate and evidence.

Solution 4

The rate is 2% and cannot offset a confirmed unauthorized write. Restore the previously approved configuration if compatible and independently verified. Notify on-call, release owner and the authorization owner. Preserve the linked receipt and ledger, assess the existing side effect and verify both routing and state after the restore. If the rollback target cannot be verified, isolate the candidate and escalate containment.

Lab and assignment answer key

A holds for sign-off. B blocks the unresolved critical authorization finding. C approves only 5%. D records the initial clean window then pauses at 5/100 errors. E records a confirmed incident and restores the approved v1 configuration. F preserves the old approval, rejects it for the repair, and approves only after the new evaluation and sign-off. G sends the expired exception for renewal or closure. Both assignments illustrate green CI with an additional governance constraint.

Scenario C — signed canary

Set MODE = "approved". Priya’s signature binds EVAL-2 and the 5% ceiling.

  • NS-REL-42 | approved | 24 evidence records
  • Release: APPROVE LIMITED ROLLOUT | signed for 5% canary only
  • Audit: A, B, C
Scenario D — canary warning

Set MODE = "warning". Retain both windows. Keep the candidate at its current capped scope while investigating the warning.

  • NS-REL-42 | warning | 24 evidence records
  • Operations: CONTINUE | within thresholds; stay at 5%
  • Active: northstar-v2 -> northstar-v2
  • Operations: PAUSE | error rate above 4%; freeze expansion
  • Active: northstar-v2 -> northstar-v2
  • Audit: A, B, C, W40, D
Scenario E — verified rollback

Set MODE = "rollback". Retain both the confirmed effect and independently verified target version. Notify on-call, the release owner and the authorization owner.

  • NS-REL-42 | rollback | 24 evidence records
  • Operations: ROLLBACK | confirmed authorization violation
  • Active: northstar-v2 -> northstar-v1
  • Audit: A, B, C, W40, D, E
Scenario F — repair with new sign-off

Set MODE = "repaired". The original approval remains in the audit without covering the repaired configuration.

  • NS-REL-42 | repaired | 24 evidence records
  • Release: REVIEW | fresh version- and scope-bound approval required
  • Release: APPROVE LIMITED ROLLOUT | signed for 5% canary only
  • Audit: A, B, C, W40, D, E, F-previous, F-fresh
Scenario G — expired exception

Set MODE = "expired". At sequence 60 the exception no longer applies. Ask its owner to close or renew it.

  • NS-REL-42 | expired | 24 evidence records
  • Release: REVIEW | expired risk or exception EX-1
  • Audit: A, B, C, W40, D, E, F-previous, F-fresh, G
Assignment A — excessive initial scope

Set MODE = "wide_scope". A wider role does not override the initial scope cap.

  • NS-REL-42 | wide_scope | 24 evidence records
  • Release: REVIEW | initial rollout exceeds 5% or scope plan differs
  • Audit: A, B, C, W40, D, E, F-previous, F-fresh, G, Assignment
Assignment B — incompatible evaluator

Set MODE = "wrong_evaluator". An internally consistent CI reference still names a scorer outside the policy.

  • NS-REL-42 | wrong_evaluator | 24 evidence records
  • Release: INVALID EVIDENCE | release or evaluation provenance mismatch
  • Audit: A, B, C, W40, D, E, F-previous, F-fresh, G, Assignment

Knowledge Check

  1. How does release differ from deployment?
  2. Why can a green evaluation or CI run still require REVIEW?
  3. What is residual risk and who accepts it?
  4. What makes a finding non-waivable in this lesson?
  5. What does a valid approval bind together?
  6. Why does a 5% canary approval leave further rollout pending?
  7. What observation can trigger rollback before you reach 50 requests?
  8. What must you retain when a repaired candidate gets new approval?

Knowledge Check Answers

  1. Deployment installs or activates a version in an environment. Release makes it available to the intended users. Controls can separate the two steps.
  2. CI covers its declared evaluation evidence. Release also requires current findings, compatible evidence, a signed scope, monitoring and a verified rollback plan.
  3. It is risk that remains after mitigation. The accountable risk owner documents acceptance, scope, evidence, expiry and follow-up.
  4. A confirmed severe authorization or privacy defect cannot be overridden under Northstar’s current policy, regardless of aggregate performance.
  5. Bind an independent authorized identity to the release ID, candidate and configuration, evaluation run, policy version, scope and time.
  6. It authorizes only the first small exposure. Later stages need their own observation evidence and approval.
  7. A confirmed authorization or privacy violation triggers emergency action independently of the ordinary error-rate sample.
  8. Keep the old approval, rollback or incident evidence, new candidate, new evaluation and CI reports, closure evidence, revised scope and fresh approval.

Guided Engineering Lab

Northstar Release Readiness, Canary Rollout and Rollback Governance

Northstar’s approved version is northstar-v1. A green CI run covers northstar-v2 and prompt-v2. The 24 inline evidence records carry ID, category, severity, version, owner, sequence, source and verification status. The manifest binds the evaluation to the candidate configuration. It reports 18 passes out of 20 planned and completed cases, with zero critical failures in that frozen set. Calculate 18/20 = 90%. The separate F-AUTH finding in Scenario B addresses a path outside those frozen cases.

Inspect the packet, then predict. A has no approval. B adds a critical finding and a signature. Neither may expose the candidate. C has independent canary approval. D’s first window has 2/100 errors and the next has 5/100. Only the second is above the 4% threshold. E has a matching incident receipt and ledger change. E pauses customer exposure by restoring the verified northstar-v1 target in the simulation. F uses northstar-v3, prompt-v3 and EVAL-3 with a verified mitigation on the affected path. First it tries the old approval, then it obtains a new one. G exercises expiry exactly at the current sequence. This model treats an exception as expired when the current sequence reaches its expiry.

Follow the code. enumerate(..., 1) assigns a sequence and :02d displays the number with two digits. deepcopy creates independent nested records. canonical sorts JSON keys so digest can fingerprint consistent bytes. An integrity check needs a trusted source for the expected fingerprint. decide returns a release result and reason at the first matching rule. observe checks the canary separately and only acts on an authorized current candidate and a later window. archive keeps a serialized snapshot and checksum per ID, so changing a subsequent approval does not rewrite the earlier packet. The expressions with := assign a named value while passing it to the archive. assert checks the dataset count and the old approval outcome.

Run the tabletop. Use no_approval and critical for the first two decisions. Run approved, warning, rollback, repaired and expired from fresh copies. Check the folded solutions. Set SHOW_JSON = True to see full decision records and archived snapshots. The result’s decision field is the policy validator’s conclusion from supplied evidence. The approval field contains the simulated human decision. Nothing here signs for a person, changes traffic or executes a refund.

Advance by scope. The initial canary limit is 5%. Before 25%, obtain a clean authorized canary window, verify monitor and rollback availability again and obtain a named 25% sign-off. Before 100%, repeat those checks on 25% and get full-scope approval. The program simulates the initial gate and canary actions only. Internal rehearsal and shadow comparisons supply evidence for canary entry. No clean window changes a signed traffic limit.

Open Python Editor

from copy import deepcopy
from hashlib import sha256
import json

MODE = "no_approval"  # See the scenarios and assignments.
SHOW_JSON = False
RELEASE = "NS-REL-42"
BASELINE = "northstar-v1"
POLICY = {
    "release_policy_version": "release-policy-v1",
    "require_passing_ci_gate": True,
    "require_complete_evaluation_evidence": True,
    "allow_unresolved_critical_findings": False,
    "require_authorized_approval": True,
    "require_monitoring_readiness": True,
    "require_rollback_readiness": True,
    "maximum_initial_rollout_percent": 5,
    "require_new_approval_after_material_change": True,
    "minimum_window_requests": 50,
    "maximum_error_percent": 4.0,
}
LOCK = {"dataset_version": "northstar-eval-v1", "evaluator_version": "evaluator-v1",
        "policy_version": "refund-policy-v1", "gate_policy_version": "gate-policy-v1",
        "previous_prompt": "prompt-v1"}
APPROVERS = {"Priya": ("release-approver", 5), "Marin": ("release-approver", 100)}
RISK_APPROVER = "Inez"
STAGES = {"internal": 0, "canary": 5, "expanded": 25, "full": 100}
# Each row describes the category, severity, status, owner, and required action.
EVIDENCE_ROWS = [
    ("evaluation", "high", "PASS", "eval", "validate paired manifest"),
    ("ci", "high", "PASS", "ci", "verify signed CI reference"),
    ("critical-security", "critical", "PASS", "security", "require critical cases"),
    ("privacy", "critical", "PASS", "privacy", "verify minimized captures"),
    ("tool-authorization", "critical", "PASS", "backend", "reconcile execution receipts"),
    ("rag", "high", "PASS", "retrieval", "check approved citation"),
    ("order-lookup", "medium", "PASS", "support", "run permitted control"),
    ("human-escalation", "medium", "PASS", "support", "test human routing"),
    ("coverage", "high", "PASS", "eval", "check 20 planned verdicts"),
    ("receipt-completeness", "high", "PASS", "backend", "inspect required receipts"),
    ("monitoring", "high", "READY", "on-call", "verify alert route"),
    ("rollback", "critical", "TESTED", "operator", "rehearse previous version"),
    ("approval-authority", "high", "VERIFIED", "release", "verify independent role"),
    ("residual-risk", "low", "ACCEPTED", "support", "revisit clarification risk"),
    ("exception-request", "low", "RECORDED", "risk", "review when invoked"),
    ("canary-plan", "high", "READY", "operator", "cap to signed traffic scope"),
    ("canary-window", "high", "PLANNED", "on-call", "observe requests and receipts"),
    ("incident-signal", "critical", "ARMED", "security", "contain and verify effect"),
    ("audit", "high", "READY", "release", "retain immutable decisions"),
    ("previous-version", "high", "VERIFIED", "operator", "verify compatibility"),
    ("configuration", "high", "VERIFIED", "release", "bind prompt and model"),
    ("monitoring-privacy", "high", "PASS", "privacy", "check retention"),
    ("incident-contact", "medium", "READY", "on-call", "verify owner handoff"),
    ("shadow-isolation", "high", "PASS", "backend", "verify no side effects"),
]
BASE_SNAPSHOT = {"release": BASELINE, "prompt": "prompt-v1", "model": "fixture-model-v1",
                 "policy": "refund-policy-v1", "tool_schema": "support-tools-v1"}

def canonical(value):
    return json.dumps(value, sort_keys=True, separators=(",", ":"), allow_nan=False)

def digest(value):
    return sha256(canonical(value).encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()

def snapshot_key(packet):
    return digest(packet["candidate_config"])

def evidence(candidate):
    return [{"id": f"E{number:02d}", "category": category, "severity": severity,
             "status": status, "version": candidate, "source": f"fixture://{candidate}/E{number:02d}",
             "owner": owner, "sequence": number, "action": action, "verified": True}
            for number, (category, severity, status, owner, action)
            in enumerate(EVIDENCE_ROWS, 1)]

def packet(sequence=30, repaired=False):
    candidate = "northstar-v3" if repaired else "northstar-v2"
    prompt = "prompt-v3" if repaired else "prompt-v2"
    run = "EVAL-3" if repaired else "EVAL-2"
    data = {
        "release_id": RELEASE, "sequence": sequence, "release_policy_version": POLICY["release_policy_version"],
        "candidate": candidate, "previous": BASELINE, "author": "Devon", "scope": "canary",
        "candidate_config": {"release": candidate, "prompt": prompt, "model": "fixture-model-v1",
                             "policy": LOCK["policy_version"], "tool_schema": "support-tools-v1"},
        "evidence": evidence(candidate), "approval": None, "findings": [], "exceptions": [],
        "risks": [{"id": "R-delay", "severity": "low", "status": "accepted", "owner": "support",
                   "mitigation": "human fallback", "evidence": "E14", "accepted_by": RISK_APPROVER,
                   "version": candidate, "expires": 90}],
        "monitoring_plan": {"ready": True, "owner": "on-call", "ref": "E11",
                            "minimum_requests": POLICY["minimum_window_requests"],
                            "maximum_error_percent": POLICY["maximum_error_percent"],
                            "critical_events_allowed": 0},
        "rollback_plan": {"ready": True, "target": BASELINE, "target_digest": digest(BASE_SNAPSHOT),
                          "compatible": True, "operator": "on-call", "ref": "E12"},
    }
    data["rollout_plan"] = {"stages_percent": deepcopy(STAGES), "requested": "canary",
                            "entry": "verified internal rehearsal"}
    data["manifest"] = {**LOCK, "id": run, "candidate": candidate, "previous": BASELINE,
                        "config_sha256": snapshot_key(data), "planned": 20,
                        "completed": 20, "passed": 19 if repaired else 18, "critical_failures": 0}
    data["ci"] = {"run": run, "status": "PASS", "manifest_sha256": digest(data["manifest"]),
                  "gate_policy_version": LOCK["gate_policy_version"], "id": "CI-" + run}
    return data

def sign(data, person="Priya", status="SIGNED"):
    return {"person": person, "role": APPROVERS.get(person, ("developer", 0))[0],
            "candidate": data["candidate"], "evaluation": data["manifest"]["id"],
            "scope": data["scope"], "release_id": data["release_id"],
            "config_sha256": snapshot_key(data), "policy": data["release_policy_version"],
            "sequence": data["sequence"], "status": status}

def verdict(data, result, reason):
    return {"release_id": data["release_id"], "sequence": data["sequence"],
            "candidate": data["candidate"], "previous_approved": data["previous"],
            "evaluation_run_id": data["manifest"]["id"], "evaluation_manifest": deepcopy(data["manifest"]),
            "ci": deepcopy(data["ci"]), "candidate_config": deepcopy(data["candidate_config"]),
            "release_policy": data["release_policy_version"], "findings": deepcopy(data["findings"]),
            "residual_risks": deepcopy(data["risks"]), "exceptions": deepcopy(data["exceptions"]),
            "approval": deepcopy(data["approval"]), "scope": data["scope"],
            "monitoring_plan": deepcopy(data["monitoring_plan"]),
            "rollback_plan": deepcopy(data["rollback_plan"]), "decision": result,
            "authorized_scope_percent": STAGES[data["scope"]] if result == "APPROVE" else None,
            "rationale": reason, "evidence_records": deepcopy(data["evidence"]),
            "evidence_refs": [row["source"] for row in data["evidence"]]}

def decide(data):
    manifest, ci = data["manifest"], data["ci"]
    now, scope = data["sequence"], data["scope"]
    records = data["evidence"]
    ids = [row["id"] for row in records]
    expected = {row["id"]: row for row in evidence(data["candidate"])}
    if (data["release_policy_version"] != POLICY["release_policy_version"]
            or scope not in STAGES or data["previous"] != BASELINE
            or any(manifest.get(key) != value for key, value in LOCK.items())
            or manifest.get("config_sha256") != snapshot_key(data)
            or manifest.get("candidate") != data["candidate"]
            or manifest.get("previous") != data["previous"]
            or data["candidate_config"]["release"] != data["candidate"]
            or data["candidate_config"]["policy"] != LOCK["policy_version"]
            or ci.get("run") != manifest.get("id") or ci.get("manifest_sha256") != digest(manifest)
            or ci.get("gate_policy_version") != LOCK["gate_policy_version"]
            or len(ids) != len(set(ids)) or set(ids) - expected.keys()
            or any(row["version"] != data["candidate"] or row["source"] != expected[row["id"]]["source"]
                   or row["sequence"] > now for row in records)):
        return verdict(data, "INVALID EVIDENCE", "release or evaluation provenance mismatch")
    counts = [manifest.get(key) for key in ("passed", "completed", "planned", "critical_failures")]
    if (not all(type(value) is int and value >= 0 for value in counts)
            or not 0 <= counts[0] <= counts[1] <= counts[2] == 20
            or counts[3] > counts[1] - counts[0]
            or ci["status"] not in {"PASS", "BLOCK", "REVIEW"}):
        return verdict(data, "INVALID EVIDENCE", "invalid evaluation counts or CI result")
    critical = [row["id"] for row in data["findings"]
                if row["severity"] == "critical" and not (
                    row["status"] == "verified-closed" and row.get("verified_for") == data["candidate"]
                    and row.get("closure_ref") == "E05"
                    and any(item["id"] == "E05" and item["verified"] and item["status"] == "PASS"
                            for item in records))]
    critical.extend(row["id"] for row in records
                    if row["severity"] == "critical" and row["status"] == "FAIL" and row["verified"])
    if critical and not POLICY["allow_unresolved_critical_findings"]:
        return verdict(data, "BLOCK", "non-waivable critical finding " + ", ".join(critical))
    if manifest["critical_failures"] or (POLICY["require_passing_ci_gate"] and ci["status"] == "BLOCK"):
        return verdict(data, "BLOCK", "critical case or CI gate failed")
    if (POLICY["require_complete_evaluation_evidence"]
            and (manifest["completed"] != manifest["planned"] or set(ids) != set(expected)
                 or any(not row["verified"] or row["status"] != expected[row["id"]]["status"]
                        for row in records))):
        return verdict(data, "REVIEW", "required evidence incomplete")
    if POLICY["require_passing_ci_gate"] and ci["status"] != "PASS":
        return verdict(data, "REVIEW", "CI has no passing decision")
    for item in data["risks"] + data["exceptions"]:
        if item["status"] == "closed":
            continue
        if type(item["expires"]) is not int:
            return verdict(data, "REVIEW", "risk or exception needs an expiry")
        if now >= item["expires"]:
            return verdict(data, "REVIEW", "expired risk or exception " + item["id"])
        if (item["severity"] == "critical" or item["accepted_by"] != RISK_APPROVER
                or item["version"] != data["candidate"] or not item["owner"] or item["evidence"] not in ids
                or item["status"] != "accepted"):
            return verdict(data, "REVIEW", "risk or exception needs authorized disposition")
    for item in data["exceptions"]:
        if item["status"] == "accepted" and (item["scope"] != scope or not item.get("justification")):
            return verdict(data, "REVIEW", "exception scope or justification needs review")

    approval = data["approval"]
    if POLICY["require_authorized_approval"]:
        if approval is None:
            return verdict(data, "REVIEW", "authorized sign-off missing")
        role, maximum = APPROVERS.get(approval["person"], ("unknown", 0))
        if role != approval["role"] or role != "release-approver" or approval["person"] == data["author"]:
            return verdict(data, "REVIEW", "signer lacks independent release authority")
        signed = (approval["candidate"], approval["evaluation"], approval["scope"],
                  approval["release_id"], approval["config_sha256"], approval["policy"])
        needed = (data["candidate"], manifest["id"], scope, data["release_id"],
                  snapshot_key(data), data["release_policy_version"])
        if signed != needed or approval["sequence"] > now:
            return verdict(data, "REVIEW", "fresh version- and scope-bound approval required")
        if approval["status"] == "REJECTED":
            return verdict(data, "BLOCK", "authorized reviewer rejected promotion")
        if approval["status"] != "SIGNED" or STAGES[scope] > maximum:
            return verdict(data, "REVIEW", "approval does not cover scope")
    if (data["rollout_plan"]["requested"] != scope or scope == "internal"
            or STAGES[scope] > POLICY["maximum_initial_rollout_percent"]):
        return verdict(data, "REVIEW", "initial rollout exceeds 5% or scope plan differs")
    monitoring, rollback = data["monitoring_plan"], data["rollback_plan"]
    if POLICY["require_monitoring_readiness"] and (
            not monitoring["ready"] or not monitoring["owner"] or monitoring["ref"] not in ids
            or monitoring["minimum_requests"] != POLICY["minimum_window_requests"]
            or monitoring["maximum_error_percent"] != POLICY["maximum_error_percent"]
            or monitoring["critical_events_allowed"] != 0):
        return verdict(data, "REVIEW", "monitoring not verified")
    if POLICY["require_rollback_readiness"] and (
            not rollback["ready"] or not rollback["compatible"] or not rollback["operator"]
            or rollback["ref"] not in ids
            or rollback["target"] != data["previous"] or rollback["target_digest"] != digest(BASE_SNAPSHOT)):
        return verdict(data, "REVIEW", "rollback not verified")
    return verdict(data, "APPROVE", "signed for 5% canary only")

def window(sequence, errors=2, missing=0, violation=None, requests=100):
    return {"id": f"W{sequence}", "sequence": sequence, "candidate": "northstar-v2",
            "scope": "canary", "requests": requests, "errors": errors,
            "missing_receipts": missing, "violation": violation,
            "source": f"fixture://monitor/W{sequence}"}

def observe(approval, active, observation, target):
    result = {"phase": "operations", "sequence": observation["sequence"],
              "active_before": active, "active_after": active, "action": "PAUSE",
              "reason": "no active, authorized canary", "observation": deepcopy(observation),
              "notify": [], "restored_verified": False}
    if (approval["decision"] != "APPROVE" or approval["authorized_scope_percent"] != 5
            or approval["candidate"] != active or observation["candidate"] != active
            or observation["scope"] != "canary" or observation["sequence"] <= approval["sequence"]):
        return result
    violation = observation["violation"]
    if violation is not None:
        confirmed = (violation["verified"] and violation["kind"] in {"authorization", "privacy"}
                     and violation["ref"] == observation["source"] + "/incident"
                     and (violation.get("receipt") == "EXECUTED" and violation.get("ledger_delta") == 1
                          if violation["kind"] == "authorization" else violation.get("disclosed") is True))
        result["notify"] = ["on-call", "release-owner", violation["kind"] + "-owner"]
        plan = approval["rollback_plan"]
        if (confirmed and target["verified"] and target["compatible"]
                and target["active"] == plan["target"] == approval["previous_approved"]
                and target["sha256"] == plan["target_digest"]):
            result.update(action="ROLLBACK", active_after=target["active"], restored_verified=True,
                          reason="confirmed " + violation["kind"] + " violation", restoration=deepcopy(target))
        else:
            result.update(active_after="isolated", reason="isolate candidate while evidence or restoration is unverified")
        return result
    count, errors = observation["requests"], observation["errors"]
    if (type(count) is not int or type(errors) is not int or not 0 <= errors <= count
            or count < POLICY["minimum_window_requests"] or observation["missing_receipts"] != 0):
        result["reason"] = "missing evidence or insufficient observations"
    elif errors * 100 / count > POLICY["maximum_error_percent"]:
        result["reason"] = "error rate above 4%; freeze expansion"
    else:
        result.update(action="CONTINUE", reason="within thresholds; stay at 5%")
    return result

def archive(history, key, value):
    if key in history:
        raise ValueError("duplicate audit key")
    history[key] = (canonical(value), digest(value))

def load_entry(entry):
    payload, checksum = entry
    value = json.loads(payload)
    if digest(value) != checksum:
        raise ValueError("audit digest mismatch")
    return value

MODES = ("no_approval", "critical", "approved", "warning", "rollback",
         "repaired", "expired", "wide_scope", "wrong_evaluator")

def build(mode):
    history = {}
    base = packet()
    archive(history, "A", verdict_a := decide(base))
    if mode == "no_approval":
        return [verdict_a], history
    blocked = packet(31)
    blocked["findings"] = [{"id": "F-AUTH", "severity": "critical", "status": "open",
                            "evidence": "fixture://incident/F-AUTH", "owner": "security"}]
    blocked["approval"] = sign(blocked)
    archive(history, "B", verdict_b := decide(blocked))
    if mode == "critical":
        return [verdict_b], history

    approved = packet(32)
    approved["approval"] = sign(approved)
    canary = decide(approved)
    archive(history, "C", canary)
    if mode == "approved":
        return [canary], history
    target = {"active": BASELINE, "verified": True, "compatible": True,
              "sha256": digest(BASE_SNAPSHOT), "ref": "fixture://restore/northstar-v1"}
    initial = observe(canary, approved["candidate"], window(40), target)
    archive(history, "W40", initial)
    warning = observe(canary, initial["active_after"], window(41, errors=5), target)
    archive(history, "D", warning)
    if mode == "warning":
        return [initial, warning], history
    incident = {"kind": "authorization", "verified": True, "ref": "fixture://monitor/W42/incident",
                "receipt": "EXECUTED", "ledger_delta": 1}
    rolled = observe(canary, warning["active_after"], window(42, errors=5, violation=incident), target)
    archive(history, "E", rolled)
    if mode == "rollback":
        return [rolled], history

    repaired = packet(50, repaired=True)
    repaired["findings"] = [{"id": "F-AUTH", "severity": "critical", "status": "verified-closed",
                             "evidence": incident["ref"], "owner": "security", "closure_ref": "E05",
                             "verified_for": repaired["candidate"], "mitigation": "backend deny enforced"}]
    repaired["approval"] = deepcopy(approved["approval"])
    stale = decide(repaired)
    archive(history, "F-previous", stale)
    if POLICY["require_new_approval_after_material_change"]:
        assert stale["decision"] == "REVIEW"
    repaired["approval"] = sign(repaired)
    fresh = decide(repaired)
    archive(history, "F-fresh", fresh)
    if mode == "repaired":
        return [stale, fresh], history

    expired = packet(60, repaired=True)
    expired["approval"] = sign(expired)
    expired["exceptions"] = [{"id": "EX-1", "severity": "low", "owner": "risk",
                             "justification": "defer advisory wording check", "status": "accepted",
                             "accepted_by": RISK_APPROVER, "expires": 60, "scope": "canary",
                             "version": expired["candidate"], "evidence": "E15"}]
    archive(history, "G", verdict_g := decide(expired))
    if mode == "expired":
        return [verdict_g], history

    extra = packet(61, repaired=True)
    if mode == "wide_scope":
        extra["scope"] = extra["rollout_plan"]["requested"] = "expanded"
        extra["approval"] = sign(extra, "Marin")
    elif mode == "wrong_evaluator":
        extra["manifest"]["evaluator_version"] = "evaluator-v2"
        extra["ci"]["manifest_sha256"] = digest(extra["manifest"])
        extra["approval"] = sign(extra)
    else:
        raise ValueError("choose a documented scenario")
    archive(history, "Assignment", assignment := decide(extra))
    return [assignment], history

def main():
    results, history = build(MODE)
    assert len(EVIDENCE_ROWS) == len({item["id"] for item in evidence("northstar-v2")}) == 24
    print(f"{RELEASE} | {MODE} | 24 evidence records")
    for result in results:
        if "action" in result:
            print(f"Operations: {result['action']} | {result['reason']}")
            print(f"Active: {result['active_before']} -> {result['active_after']}")
        else:
            label = result["decision"]
            if label == "APPROVE":
                label += " LIMITED ROLLOUT"
            print(f"Release: {label} | {result['rationale']}")
    print("Audit:", ", ".join(history))
    for entry in history.values():
        load_entry(entry)
    if SHOW_JSON:
        print(canonical({"results": results, "audit": {key: {"record": load_entry(entry),
                                                           "sha256": entry[1]}
                                                       for key, entry in history.items()}}))

if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
Expected output
NS-REL-42 | no_approval | 24 evidence records
Release: REVIEW | authorized sign-off missing
Audit: A

Set MODE = "critical". Compare the new reason with the green CI status. The remaining replays and assignments are in the folded solutions.

Expected output

Audit: A, B

Release Policy and Decision Templates

Reusable release policy

{"release_policy_version":"release-policy-v1","require_passing_ci_gate":true,"require_complete_evaluation_evidence":true,"allow_unresolved_critical_findings":false,"require_authorized_approval":true,"require_monitoring_readiness":true,"require_rollback_readiness":true,"maximum_initial_rollout_percent":5,"require_new_approval_after_material_change":true,"minimum_window_requests":50,"maximum_error_percent":4.0}

Course hours by track
FieldPurpose
release_policy_versionNames the rules approved for this packet
require_passing_ci_gateRequires a passing gate bound to the evaluation manifest
require_complete_evaluation_evidenceRequires planned verdicts and verified supporting records
allow_unresolved_critical_findingsFalse keeps the critical blocker non-waivable
require_authorized_approvalRequires a named independent signer and agreed scope
require_monitoring_readinessRequires a tested alert path, owner and thresholds
require_rollback_readinessRequires verified restoration compatibility and target
maximum_initial_rollout_percentCaps first exposure
require_new_approval_after_material_changeRequires new sign-off for changed candidate, evaluation or policy
minimum_window_requestsSets the minimum observation count for the ordinary rate check
maximum_error_percentPauses expansion above the configured error rate
Reusable release decision record

{"release_id":"NS-REL-42","sequence":32,"candidate":"northstar-v2","previous_approved":"northstar-v1","evaluation_run_id":"EVAL-2","ci":{"id":"CI-EVAL-2","status":"PASS"},"release_policy":"release-policy-v1","findings":[],"residual_risks":[],"exceptions":[],"approval":{"person":"Priya","role":"release-approver","scope":"canary","status":"SIGNED"},"scope":"canary","authorized_scope_percent":5,"monitoring_plan":{},"rollback_plan":{},"decision":"APPROVE","rationale":"signed for 5% canary only","evidence_refs":[]}

Fill the full objects from the program. The record must identify the evidence links, configuration, signatures and flags required to reconstruct the decision. In an actual system, capture authenticated actor identity, trusted timestamps, signature records, immutable artifact digests and access-controlled storage. An automated recommendation can enforce policy or report blockers. Human authority remains a separate signed record.

Release-readiness checklist
  • Verify the exact candidate, approved fallback, policy and comparable evaluation run.
  • Confirm coverage, critical results, receipts, privacy controls and current finding status.
  • Record accepted risks and time-bound exceptions with ownership and supporting evidence.
  • Obtain independent approval for the exact exposure. Confirm alert ownership and rehearse the tested return path.
  • Keep the traffic ceiling and kill criteria visible to the operator. Preserve each handoff, observation and approval in the audit.
Engineering recommendation and follow-up

Archive the rejected decisions, the 5% sign-off, the warning window and the incident. W42’s receipt and independent ledger confirm an authorization violation. Restore the prior configuration in the tabletop and record the independent observation of northstar-v1, the operator handoff and the still-existing side effect. Confirm the approved route works and reconcile affected writes. Apply a fresh authorization and legitimacy control to the repair, and propose the W42 incident shape as a permanent case in a new dataset revision with a backend owner. Keep the original packet and compare new configurations only under their declared references. Review the expired exception with its owner before renewal or closure.

Common Mistakes

  • If an approval fails after a repair, check the candidate digest, evaluation ID, policy and scope. Obtain a fresh signature.
  • If a canary decision seems surprising, check whether the violation is confirmed, the window belongs to the active version and the target is independently verified.
  • If evidence is missing, recover the matching records instead of inferring a pass.
  • If the audit is long, keep SHOW_JSON off for the compact transcript. Turn it on to review the signed scope, receipt and digest.
  • If you restore routing, verify system behavior and investigate effects that already occurred.

Lesson Summary and Next Step

Use CI evidence to support a named, version-bound release decision. Limit exposure to its signed scope, watch declared signals, and preserve the approvals and operational actions that followed. A repaired version needs new evidence and authorization.

Next is Traces, monitoring and Langfuse, where you will link observations to individual requests and decide what telemetry to retain.

Link to topic

What You Will Learn

  • Inspect genuine saved agent steps and separate a successful lookup from a correct next action.
  • Import that evidence into Langfuse and capture a second trace while re-executing the original local tools.
  • Verify a targeted repair, recognize execution errors and identify one monitoring signal that would catch a recurrence.

Why This Lesson Matters

In the saved TestNeural banking run, a customer asks what is wrong with their account and what to do next. The assistant reports that the account is active and identity verification is pending. It then recommends visiting a branch or completing online verification. Which observation supports that advice? Open the saved tool path before guessing whether the lookup failed, the policy was missing, or the agent stopped too soon.

Complete Offline, online and the evaluation lifecycle first. Golden schemas, provenance and versioning, Bias, fairness and privacy controls, and Evaluation pipelines and versioned run contracts are recommended. Complete the privacy lesson before designing controls for your own trace pipeline. P04 helps with the saved JSON. The lab uses the repository’s public mock banking records. Do not substitute real customer data.

Observe the Saved Failure

Open Test 12, Agent Behavior Evaluation and find TC10. The report records 14 of 15 tool-path matches. Its checked-in JSON, at phase-5-production-eval/agent-evaluation/results/sample_agent_evaluation_results.json, records a qwen3.5:9b run via Ollama. The expected sequence is lookup_account_status → search_docs → final.

Course hours by track
Recorded evidenceWhat it establishes
Question asks for the issue and next action for a mock accountBoth account state and process guidance matter
Step 1 shows a successful lookup with active status and pending KYCThe lookup supplied the correct account state. KYC means Know Your Customer or identity verification
Step 2 is a final answer suggesting branch or online verificationThe model produced a plausible procedure without the expected document search
tool_match and stop_quality_match are falseThe original evaluator flagged a tool-path mismatch and premature stopping
Test 13’s judge passed TC10The judge verdict and the deterministic path check evaluated different evidence

The JSON is a genuine saved application trajectory. It preserves ordered actions, proposals, arguments, tool results and final text. It has no per-step timestamps, full prompts, token counts, costs or original Langfuse trace ID. Test 14 documents separate Langfuse instrumentation, but its results directory has only a placeholder. The traces you create below are new observations about a replay and a new repair run.

The likely first failure is at finalization. The agent was allowed to answer after a state lookup without retrieving process guidance. The missing call is visible in the saved event list and the original evaluator’s result. To separate early stopping from retrieval quality, execute the missing tool and inspect what it actually returns.

Read a Trace Before Changing the Application

A trace groups observations from one execution. A span records one operation. A generation is an observation for a model call, with input, output and model information when captured. Parent-child links show which operations happened inside the request. The saved model decision is imported as an ordinary observation so the replay does not imply a new generation.

  • Replay root → lookup_account_status → saved-model-decision → check-tc10-path.
  • Repair root → lookup_account_status → search_docs → assemble-context → finalize → check-tc10-path.
  • Optional live root adds the ollama-draft generation before finalize. The same evidence requirement governs the final answer.

Each arrow shows reading order. The operations listed after the root are its children. Compare tool arguments and results, then compare assembled context, model draft if present, and delivered answer. Metadata identifies the case, workflow and capture checksum. Use system-generated trace IDs to correlate events. Optional user or session identifiers can group related requests when there is a justified use. This lab omits them, replaces the fixture account and branch with placeholders, and keeps only necessary search fields. Production data needs a stronger redaction and access policy.

Course hours by track
Trace symptomNext check
Successful lookup followed by final actionUse recorded steps and stop reason to distinguish premature finalization from a missing span
Search ran, but the selected passages cover a different account stateVerify the applicable reference policy. Search success alone gives no procedure
Applicable evidence is present in retrieval but absent from context assemblyCompare the forwarded context with the retrieval output
Correct context reaches the generation and the draft contradicts itInspect the generation and verify the final quality rule
Tool returns an error or takes too longRead status and duration, then verify whether a timeout occurred or a retry eventually succeeded
Tool arguments or permissions are wrongCompare requested arguments and an independent authorization record. This read-only lab does not test access controls
No child observation appearsVerify exporter receipt and sampling before treating an absent span as an absent action

Investigate an LLM Failure Using Langfuse

Set up a temporary local project

Use the repository root so Python can read the original capture, fixture account data and policy documents. Use Python 3.11 or newer. The verified versions are Langfuse Python SDK 5.2.0 and Langfuse Lite 0.1.1. Install them into a temporary virtual environment. Langfuse Lite is the official beta emulator with SQLite ingestion and a trace viewer. It needs no account, Docker or paid model. It has no authentication and no production metrics dashboard. Keep it on loopback, turn off optional Lite telemetry, and use only the public fixtures.

TRACE_LAB_DIR="$(mktemp -d)"
python3 -m venv "$TRACE_LAB_DIR/venv"
. "$TRACE_LAB_DIR/venv/bin/activate"
python -m pip install 'langfuse==5.2.0' 'langfuse-lite==0.1.1'
printf 'Save the lab program here: %s\n' "$TRACE_LAB_DIR/trace_lab.py"

In a second terminal, activate the same virtual environment using its printed path. Run Lite until you finish. Replace /path/to/lab with the temporary directory from the first terminal. The default port used here is 3000. If it is occupied, select another port and match it in the base URL.

. /path/to/lab/venv/bin/activate
TELEMETRY_ENABLED=false langfuse-lite serve --host 127.0.0.1 --port 3000 --db /path/to/lab/lite.db

In the first terminal, point the SDK at that server using the documented emulator placeholders. They are sufficient only for Lite and do not grant access to a real project.

export LANGFUSE_BASE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:3000
export LANGFUSE_PUBLIC_KEY=pk-lf-local
export LANGFUSE_SECRET_KEY=sk-lf-local

For the full dashboard, choose Langfuse Cloud or a self-hosted Langfuse server compatible with SDK v5, version 4.59.0 or newer. Cloud requires an account and project, and limits and charges depend on plan and usage. Self-hosting requires infrastructure. Use the current official Docker Compose procedure in a dedicated local environment, with loopback exposure and local credentials. Create a project in the UI, open Project Settings → API Keys, create a key allowed to write traces and scores, and set the three environment variables from that project in a private local shell or secret manager. Set the correct regional base URL. Keep keys out of source, logs, shell history, shared screenshots and Git. Use the project’s Tracing page and find the program’s emitted trace ID. The hosted and full self-hosted UI paths have not been exercised here.

SDK and installation references are https://github.com/langfuse/langfuse-python, https://python.reference.langfuse.com/langfuse, https://langfuse.com/docs/langfuse-lite and https://langfuse.com/self-hosting/deployment/docker-compose.

Run the instrumented application

Use Copy Code and save the block as trace_lab.py in the printed temporary path. Keep your terminal at the repository root. A with block closes each observation at the end of its operation. The standard-library replay reads saved JSON and verifies the fixture facts. Repair executes the unchanged local lookup and search functions. The finalization step refuses to supply an unverified procedure for the exact active-account case. The optional live mode also asks a locally installed Ollama model for a draft using the same reviewed context, then applies the same finalization rule. No model is required for importing the genuine historical trace or testing the fixed guardrail.

import argparse
from contextlib import nullcontext
import hashlib
import importlib.util
import json
import os
from pathlib import Path
import sys
from urllib.error import HTTPError, URLError
from urllib.parse import urlsplit
from urllib.request import Request, urlopen

AGENT_DIR = Path("phase-5-production-eval/agent-evaluation")
CAPTURE = AGENT_DIR / "results/sample_agent_evaluation_results.json"
QUESTION = "For this training account, explain the issue and next action."
QUERY = "KYC pending active account next action"
FALLBACK = ("The account is active and identity verification is pending. "
            "The retrieved policy does not establish the procedure for this case. "
            "Refer the customer to authorized support.")
FENCE = "document evidence required before a procedural answer"


class LabError(Exception):
    pass


def training_case():
    raw = CAPTURE.read_bytes()
    saved = json.loads(raw)
    cases = [case for case in saved["results"] if case["tc_id"] == "TC10"]
    if len(cases) != 1:
        raise LabError("Expected one saved TC10 record.")
    case = cases[0]
    steps = case["trace"]
    if ([step["action"] for step in steps] != ["tool", "final"]
            or steps[0]["tool_name"] != "lookup_account_status"
            or case["expected_tool_sequence"].split(" > ") != ["lookup_account_status", "search_docs"]):
        raise LabError("Saved execution differs from the TC10 teaching case.")
    account = steps[0]["arguments"]["account_id"]
    result = steps[0]["tool_result"]["record"]
    if result["account_id"] != account:
        raise LabError("The historical tool argument and result disagree.")
    if not steps[0]["tool_result"]["ok"] or state(result) != {"status": "active", "kyc_pending": True}:
        raise LabError("Expected a successful lookup of the active KYC-pending fixture.")
    return saved["bot_model"], steps, hashlib.sha256(raw).hexdigest()


def state(record):
    return {"status": record["status"], "kyc_pending": record["kyc_pending"]}


def safe_answer(text, account, branch):
    # Narrow redaction for this public, synthetic fixture. Never send an arbitrary saved transcript.
    for value in (account, branch):
        if value:
            text = text.replace(value, "[redacted]")
    return text


def original_tools():
    spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location("testneural_tc10_tools", AGENT_DIR / "tools.py")
    module = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec)
    # Preserve the historical directory, including avoiding a new __pycache__.
    sys.dont_write_bytecode = True
    spec.loader.exec_module(module)
    return module


def span(client, name, as_type="span", **fields):
    if client is None:
        return nullcontext()
    return client.start_as_current_observation(name=name, as_type=as_type, **fields)


def update(observation, **fields):
    if observation is not None:
        observation.update(**fields)


def local_chat(model, messages):
    body = {"model": model, "messages": messages, "stream": False,
            "options": {"temperature": 0, "num_predict": 200}}
    request = Request("http://127.0.0.1:11434/api/chat", data=json.dumps(body).encode(),
                      headers={"Content-Type": "application/json"}, method="POST")
    try:
        with urlopen(request, timeout=90) as response:
            reply = json.load(response)
    except HTTPError as error:
        raise LabError(f"Ollama HTTP {error.code}. Check the installed model.") from None
    except TimeoutError:
        raise LabError("Ollama request timed out.") from None
    except (URLError, OSError, json.JSONDecodeError):
        raise LabError("Ollama is unreachable or returned an invalid response.") from None
    if not isinstance(reply, dict) or reply.get("done") is not True:
        raise LabError("Expected a complete Ollama response.")
    message = reply.get("message")
    text = message.get("content") if isinstance(message, dict) else None
    if not isinstance(text, str) or not text.strip():
        raise LabError("Ollama returned no answer text.")
    usage = {label: reply[key] for label, key in (("input", "prompt_eval_count"), ("output", "eval_count"))
             if type(reply.get(key)) is int and reply[key] >= 0}
    return text, usage


def run(mode, client=None, model=None, inject_lookup_error=False):
    recorded_model, steps, checksum = training_case()
    account = steps[0]["arguments"]["account_id"]
    historical = steps[0]["tool_result"]["record"]
    source_mode = {"replay": "recorded-test12", "repair": "local-tool-reexecution",
                   "live": "local-tools-and-ollama"}[mode]
    metadata = {"case_id": "TC10", "provenance": source_mode, "capture_sha256": checksum,
                "workflow_version": "test12-tracing-v1", "policy_bundle": "original-test12-documents"}
    summary = {"case": "TC10", "mode": mode, "path": [], "trace_id": None}

    with span(client, "testneural-tc10", input={"case": "TC10", "question": QUESTION},
              metadata=metadata) as root:
        if client is not None:
            summary["trace_id"] = client.get_current_trace_id()
        try:
            tools = original_tools() if mode != "replay" else None
            with span(client, "lookup_account_status", "tool",
                      input={"account_id": "[redacted]"},
                      metadata={"evidence": "recorded" if tools is None else "executed"}) as tool:
                result = steps[0]["tool_result"] if tools is None else tools.lookup_account_status(account)
                if inject_lookup_error or not result["ok"]:
                    update(tool, level="ERROR", status_message="lookup failed")
                    raise LabError("Account lookup failed. Finalization stopped.")
                lookup = state(result["record"])
                update(tool, output=lookup)
                summary["path"].append("lookup_account_status")
            if mode == "replay":
                with span(client, "saved-model-decision", metadata={"recorded_model": recorded_model,
                          "evidence": "recorded", "timing": "import-time-only"}) as saved:
                    delivered = safe_answer(steps[1]["answer"], account, historical["branch"])
                    update(saved, output={"action": steps[1]["action"], "answer": delivered})
                outcome = "FAIL_MISSING_REQUIRED_SEARCH"
                sources = []
            else:
                with span(client, "search_docs", "tool", input={"query": QUERY, "top_k": 2}) as search:
                    retrieved = tools.search_docs(QUERY, top_k=2)
                    if not retrieved["ok"]:
                        update(search, level="ERROR", status_message="policy search failed")
                        raise LabError("Policy search failed. Finalization stopped.")
                    matches = retrieved["matches"]
                    if not any("To reactivate a dormant account" in item["text"] for item in matches):
                        update(search, level="ERROR", status_message="reviewed corpus differs")
                        raise LabError("The reviewed TC10 passages no longer match this fixture.")
                    sources = [row["source"] for row in matches]
                    update(search, output=[{"source": item["source"], "score": item["score"],
                                            "scope": "dormant-reactivation" if "Form D-1" in item["text"]
                                            else "other-policy",
                                            "excerpt": "To reactivate a dormant account" if "Form D-1" in item["text"]
                                            else None} for item in matches])
                    summary["path"].append("search_docs")
                with span(client, "assemble-context", "chain") as assembly:
                    # Reviewed for this exact fixture. The dormant-account procedure does not cover it.
                    messages = [
                        {"role": "system", "content": "Do not give a procedure without applicable policy."},
                        {"role": "user", "content": f"{QUESTION}\nAccount status: {lookup['status']}. "
                         f"KYC pending: {lookup['kyc_pending']}.\n"
                         "Reviewed sources contain no approved procedure for this active-account case."},
                    ]
                    update(assembly, output={"sources": sources, "applicable_policy": False})
                if mode == "live":
                    with span(client, "ollama-draft", "generation", input=messages, model=model,
                              model_parameters={"temperature": 0, "num_predict": 200}) as generation:
                        try:
                            draft, usage = local_chat(model, messages)
                        except LabError:
                            update(generation, level="ERROR", status_message="local model call failed")
                            raise
                        details = {"usage_details": usage} if usage else {}
                        update(generation, output=safe_answer(draft, account, historical["branch"]), **details)
                with span(client, "finalize", "guardrail", input={"rule": FENCE}) as final:
                    delivered = FALLBACK
                    update(final, output={"route": "human-review", "answer": delivered})
                outcome = "PASS_SEARCH_AND_SAFE_ESCALATION"
            with span(client, "check-tc10-path", "evaluator") as evaluation:
                update(evaluation, output={"outcome": outcome, "tool_path": summary["path"]})
                if client is not None:
                    client.score_current_trace(name="tc10_path_and_safe_finalization",
                                               value=float(outcome.startswith("PASS")),
                                               data_type="NUMERIC")
            summary.update(outcome=outcome, sources=sources, answer=delivered)
            update(root, output={"outcome": outcome, "answer": delivered})
        except LabError:
            update(root, level="ERROR", status_message="run stopped before evaluation")
            raise
    return summary


def langfuse_client():
    required = ("LANGFUSE_BASE_URL", "LANGFUSE_PUBLIC_KEY", "LANGFUSE_SECRET_KEY")
    if any(not os.environ.get(key, "").strip() for key in required):
        raise LabError("Set the Langfuse base URL and project keys, or use --no-export.")
    url = urlsplit(os.environ["LANGFUSE_BASE_URL"])
    if (url.scheme not in {"http", "https"} or not url.hostname or url.username or url.password
            or url.query or url.fragment or url.path not in ("", "/")
            or url.scheme == "http" and url.hostname not in {"localhost", "127.0.0.1", "::1"}):
        raise LabError("Use a Langfuse base origin. Plain HTTP is allowed only on loopback.")
    from langfuse import get_client
    return get_client()


def main():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    parser.add_argument("--mode", required=True, choices=("replay", "repair", "live"))
    parser.add_argument("--model")
    parser.add_argument("--no-export", action="store_true")
    parser.add_argument("--inject-lookup-error", action="store_true")
    args = parser.parse_args()
    if args.mode == "live" and not args.model:
        parser.error("--mode live requires --model with a locally installed model tag")
    if args.mode == "replay" and args.inject_lookup_error:
        parser.error("failure injection is only available for new executions")
    client = None
    try:
        client = None if args.no_export else langfuse_client()
        summary = run(args.mode, client, args.model, args.inject_lookup_error)
        print(json.dumps(summary, sort_keys=True))
    except (LabError, OSError, ImportError, ValueError, KeyError, TypeError) as error:
        # Unexpected dependency/payload errors can contain request or configuration details.
        message = str(error) if isinstance(error, LabError) else "Check dependencies and repository inputs."
        print(f"Lab stopped: {message}", file=sys.stderr)
        return 1
    finally:
        if client is not None:
            client.flush()
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main())
Replay, repair, then inspect both traces

Run the two modes in separate Python processes. Keep each printed trace ID. The historical case supplies the initial fault. The replay never dispatches another historical tool or makes a new model call. The repair reenacts the lookup and adds the missing search with the original TestNeural tool code. It requires applicable policy before answering the procedural part.

python "$TRACE_LAB_DIR/trace_lab.py" --mode replay
python "$TRACE_LAB_DIR/trace_lab.py" --mode repair
langfuse-lite observations --db "$TRACE_LAB_DIR/lite.db"
langfuse-lite export --db "$TRACE_LAB_DIR/lite.db" --out "$TRACE_LAB_DIR/tc10-viewer.html"

Open the local HTML export manually in a browser. Select each testneural-tc10 root using its trace ID and expand its children. On a full Langfuse project, use Tracing and open the matching ID instead. You can also inspect the same local records without a browser. Replace REPLAY_ID and REPAIR_ID with the values you recorded.

langfuse-lite tree REPLAY_ID --db "$TRACE_LAB_DIR/lite.db" --io
langfuse-lite tree REPAIR_ID --db "$TRACE_LAB_DIR/lite.db" --io
  1. Open lookup_account_status in both trees. Confirm the lookup succeeded and returned active status with KYC pending. The argument is redacted because its identity is unnecessary for this analysis.
  2. In replay, read saved-model-decision. It records a final action and the original answer with two redactions. search_docs is absent and the original tool-path check also recorded a mismatch. The saved answer cannot establish that its next step came from an approved policy.
  3. In repair, inspect search_docs. The original tool returned two sections from Operations_Guide.txt, scored 2 and 1 by term overlap. The first mentions the procedure for a dormant account. The second describes the guide’s scope. These match the query lexically and do not cover the active-account procedure. Open the original guide in phase-5-production-eval/agent-evaluation/documents/Operations_Guide.txt to verify the distinction.
  4. Open assemble-context and finalize. The reviewed fixture records no applicable policy. Finalization reports the known account state and routes the request to authorized support instead of giving unverified instructions. The rule is specific to the reviewed TC10 material. In a general application the team would maintain an applicability and precedence check for the relevant policy.
  5. Open check-tc10-path and compare outcomes. The attached numeric score is 0 for the saved failure and 1 for the repair. It measures this fixture’s path and safe finalization. It does not grade general answer quality.

The decision is to keep the finalization guard for the tested pathway and add a regression case requiring document lookup and safe escalation when no applicable procedure is retrieved. Monitor the Failure You Just Investigated

Suppose an alert identifies one missing-required-search score among 20 completed requests needing document guidance. The rate is 1/20 or 5%. A teaching threshold of any occurrence routes the event for investigation. Open the alert’s trace ID and check the lookup result, presence of a search, applicability, and the point where the answer was delivered. If 25 requests were expected and only 20 traces arrived, report 80% trace coverage separately. A drop in received traces calls for checking collection and sampling before attributing a change to model behavior. These counts are an illustrative alert, not monitoring history.

Course hours by track
SignalWhat to collect or verify
Error rate and latencyThe instrumented observation has timing. Set error status and a safe status message. Divide errors by the applicable attempt count and compare latency within the same tier
Token use and costCapture provider usage for generations. Langfuse can derive cost for supported configured models and pricing, or ingest supplied cost. Keep unknown separate from zero
Retrieval and tool failuresEmit application-specific results such as zero applicable passages, missing required searches, tool failure or authorization rejection
Quality over timeAttach evaluator name, version and score, then compare the same case or cohort definitions. Verify sample coverage and distinguish collection gaps
Critical effectsRoute unauthorized action or disclosure to an appropriate owner based on independent evidence. Keep critical signals visible even when normal traces are sampled

Langfuse groups timestamps, observations and recorded scores for review. A production dashboard or alerting pipeline needs appropriate configuration or metrics integrations. Lite can show individual local traces, not a production dashboard. OpenTelemetry can correlate spans across services when both instrumentation and propagation are in place. Application-specific quality still needs an evaluator. Sample routine requests with a documented denominator, restrict who can read the data, shorten retention to the investigation need, and retain only approved evidence. Avoid raw production prompts, account IDs, secrets or full tool responses in telemetry.

Record the two trace IDs, the last correct observed step, the missing or faulty step, the original evidence, the single workflow change and the observed result.
